On Fri, Feb 26, 2027 at 09:24 Naomi Feldman <naomi@redwood.com> wrote:
> Folks — Greenlane (GD-1738) is seeing a production spike: elevated 504s/429s and long tail latency.

Quick findings from the initial dump and live metrics:
- Batch queue depth on GPU pool A-03 grew ~x6 in the 08:48–08:55 window. Throughput stayed nominal but batch formation latency increased.
- KV prefix cache evictions spiked at the same time (eviction rate up >400%). There are repeated cache misses for the same prefixes: looks like a prefix eviction / re-population loop.
- There's evidence of long-lived in-flight requests holding small prefix locks while waiting for batching windows; that prevents other requests from hitting cached KV and forces regeneration. Combined effect: more KV misses -> more compute -> batch backlog -> timeouts -> retries.

Mitigation idea I applied locally (non-prod test): 1) widen batching window by +15ms, 2) increase cache TTL for hot prefixes, 3) limit per-prefix outstanding requests to 8. In test that reduced miss amplification and batch latency.

Attached: batch-trace-02-26.txt (batch timing slices + eviction logs).

I recommend we do a quick config patch to broaden the batching window and apply a temporary TTL bump for Greenlane's model route while we root cause the eviction interlock.

-marcus
Senior SRE, Serving Runtime
From: Monica Patel <monica@redwood.com>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.com>

Date: Fri, 26 Feb 2027 10:12:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Fwd: Re: sudden 504s on /v1/generate - live right now

On Fri, Feb 26, 2027 at 09:45 Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com> wrote:
> There's evidence of long-lived in-flight requests holding small prefix locks while waiting for batching windows; that prevents other requests from hitting cached KV and forces regeneration.

I pushed a temporary config change to Greenlane's routing profile:
- batching_window_ms: +15 (from 6 -> 21)
- per_prefix_outstanding: 8 -> 6 (throttle to reduce regeneration fanout)
- cache.hot_ttl_override: +45s for the route (warm hot prefixes)

Preliminary effect: error rate down from ~9% -> ~2.4% and p95 latency fell ~30% in the last 12 minutes. We still see intermittent 504s on very large sequences (their billing calls), likely due to per-request compute skew.

Next steps:
- Roll back any optimizer code change rolled in last 48 hours if we continue to see blips. Aditya, can you confirm if a rollout touched prefix eviction logic?
- Prepare a targeted canary to validate a fix for the prefix-lock race.

-Monica
Principal Engineer, Serving Runtime Ops

Immediate ask: if you can hold non-essential traffic (bulk batch jobs, scheduled syncs) for ~90 minutes, that will help us validate a full fix without a rolling rollback.
